target_task.text: Eliciting latent factual and reasoning knowledge from large language models that is not faithfully reflected in their surface-level outputs.

limitation.text: Existing approaches rely on contrastive activation patterns that struggle with complex multi-step reasoning tasks, and mechanistic tools are typically used only to understand model behavior rather than extract hidden knowledge.

combination.text: By unifying sparse autoencoder feature analysis and activation patching, the framework locates internal knowledge-bearing representations within large language models, verifies them via causal probing, and applies representation engineering to elicit hidden knowledge without modifying model weights.

summary.text: This briefing examines a framework that combines sparse autoencoder feature analysis, activation patching, and large language models to elicit latent factual and reasoning knowledge that is not faithfully reflected in surface-level outputs. Existing approaches struggle with complex multi-step reasoning tasks and treat mechanistic tools purely as analytical aids rather than extraction mechanisms. By unifying sparse autoencoders and activation patching, the system locates knowledge-bearing representations, verifies them through causal probing, and surfaces hidden knowledge without altering model weights.

target_user.text: The target user comprises software security and AI engineering teams working within corporate environments, as indicated by patent assignee categories focused on generative artificial intelligence-driven software fixing pipelines.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is that enterprise users will actively demand a specialized latent knowledge elicitation tool instead of relying on standard prompt engineering or model fine-tuning.

mvp.text: A demand landing page and problem interviews targeting AI security and engineering teams to evaluate interest in non-weight-modifying latent knowledge elicitation, testing the assumption that users face operational friction from unfaithful model outputs.
mvp.type: demand landing page and problem interviews

success_metric.text: Achieving a proposed threshold of 25 percent conversion from landing page visitors to booked problem discovery interviews, as motivated by DVF axis scores.

kill_criteria.text: Failing to secure a proposed threshold of 5 completed user interviews within 3 weeks of launching the landing page.
Finding that a proposed threshold of 80 percent of interviewed engineers report no operational need to extract unstated latent knowledge.

Used to measure the depth of model internal states via activation patching techniques.
Used for automated benchmarking of agent and model tasks on real-world software security workflows.

to_build.text: A representation engineering pipeline that couples sparse autoencoder feature localization with activation patching to extract latent knowledge without modifying underlying model weights.
